MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 8, 2020
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on September 8, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on September 3, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Acting Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  September 8, 2020
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no Closed Session to report this evening
which proved to be beneficial since there were technical difficulties. He stated that the minutes
from the August 25 City Council Meeting will be amended to add a public comment that was
inadvertently omitted.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. I-5 Widening Project Update by the Orange County Transportation Authority
  (OCTA)

  Received presentation from OCTA Program Manager Niall Barrett.

NEW BUSINESS (item #16 was taken out of order with Council consensus)

16. I-5 Sound Wall (CIP 20242) - OCTA Cooperative Agreement

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, authorize
  the City Manager to approve Cooperative Agreement No. C-0-2543 between Orange County
  Transportation Authority and the City of Mission Viejo for the design of a sound wall along
  Interstate 5.

  Council Member Sachs stated that he was abstaining because he did not feel he had enough
  information to vote yes or no on the item.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Sachs

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Brenda Cooper, M.V.: Complained that the candidate signs have become a distraction while driving
in the City and asked that candidates follow the rules.

The following complained specifically to Council Candidate Schlicht’s placement of her signs in
prohibited areas: Pam Smith, M.V.; Daniel Avery, M.V.; Cynthia Cantrelle, M.V.; Victoria Avery,
M.V.; Carol Pifer, M.V.; Beverly Montrella, M.V.; and Donna Snow, M.V.

City Council Minutes  2  September 8, 2020
 Michael Fate, M.V.: Inquired when the Montanoso Recreation Center will reopen now that the
County has been moved to the Red Zone which allows gyms to open with limited capacity.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned the City Attorney on a violation of the Brown Act at the July 14
City Council Meeting when hers and Larry Gilbert’s public comments were not read until after the
item was approved. She also stated that her late comments at the August 25 Council Meeting were
not part of the minutes.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: Recognized and gave thanks to Lieutenant Vuong, Homeless Outreach
Sergeant Kiltz, and Deputies Grumbles and Duran for assisting a homeless mother and daughter to
find housing through the Illumination Foundation. She also gave kudos to City Staff members,
Wayne Mackey, Brian Zahn and Cory Gonyea for taking time out of their Holiday Weekend to
transport the ladies’ belongings to storage. Lastly, she thanked Aegean Heights Board members,
Tamara Aguilar and Jim Hayes for going out of their way to get the pair the help they needed.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 25, 2020, as amended.

2.  Check Register Dated August 14, 2020 in the Amount of $2,626,142.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated August 21, 2020 in the Amount of $923,922.35

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2019/20

  Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2019/20.

5.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for
  Fiscal Year 2019/20

  Received and filed the accompanying CDFA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2019/20.
6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA)Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2019/20
City Council Minutes  3  September 8, 2020
   Received and filed the accompanying MVHA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2019/20.

7.  FY 2020/21 Investment Policies

  Adopted Resolution 20-41 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY 2020/21, CDFA
  Resolution 20-02 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy for FY 2020/21, and Housing
  Authority Resolution 20-03 Approving the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Investment
  Policy for FY 2020/21.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2020

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2020

  Received and filed.

10. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for July 2020

  Received and filed.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2020

  Received and filed.

12. Acceptance of Parcel Map 2020-133

  (1) Approved Parcel Map 2020-133 and authorize the City Clerk and the City Engineer to sign
  the record map upon completion of any technical corrections required by the City Engineer;
  (2) authorized the City Manager to reduce the City's Map Plan Check Overhead Percentage
  from 36% to 10% for this Parcel Map review.

13. General Plan Amendment GPA2020-33 / Zone Change ZC2020-23 / Planned
  Development Permit PDP2020-313 / Variance VAR2020-55 / and Tentative Tract Map
  TTM19035 - Petitions submitted by Trumark Homes to permit residential development
  on 6.36 acres of a 13.4-acre open space site located on El Toro Road, between Marguerite
  Parkway and the State Route 241 Toll Road (APN 839-273-04 and partial area of APN
  839-273-03). The subject property would be rezoned from R (Recreation) to RPD 30
  (Residential Planned Development) to accommodate a new residential project with 91
  for-sale dwelling units, clustered in ten 3-story buildings, with an overall project density
  of 14.3 du/ac. Variance VAR2020-55 is requested to allow reduced distance between
  buildings and alternative parking space configurations including both tandem and
  unenclosed resident parking

City Council Minutes  4  September 8, 2020
   Adopted Ordinance 20-339 Approving Zone Change ZC2020-23, being a petition submitted
  by Trumark Homes to change the Zoning Map Designation from R (Recreation) to RPD 30
  (Residential Planned Development), for 6.36 acres of property located on El Toro Road,
  between Marguerite Parkway and the State Route 241 Toll Road, and further described as
  assessor parcel number 839-273-04 and 839-273-03 (portion).

14. Alicia Parkway, Jeronimo Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation
  (CIP 21837)

  Approved Construction Contract Change Order 1 to PO 22100122 to All American Asphalt
  in the amount of $99,425 for additional work.

15. Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center Flooring Rehabilitation

  Approved first amendment for Shaw Industries, Inc. DBA Shaw Integrated Solutions for
  additional materials for the floor rehabilitation project at Norman P. Murray Community and
  Senior Center for period of June 23, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not to exceed
  $165,031.53.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS (continued)

17. Renaming of Casta Del Sol Golf Course

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to rename
  the Casta del Sol Golf Course to Oso Creek Golf Course.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

18. Annual Walk Against Drugs Event; 2020’s Virtual "Walk"; Program and Request for
  Awards Support for K-12 Student Participants

  Crime Prevention Specialist Paula Monical presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to support
  the Virtual 2020 Walk Against Drugs and allocate not more than $10,500 to the event.

City Council Minutes  5  September 8, 2020
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

20.  Update on Promoting Diversity and Inclusion

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked Police Services personnel and the residents that stepped up in
response to the homeless mother and daughter. She gave kudos to Lieutenant Vuong and former
Mayor Rhonda Reardon, and she also thanked the staff that support our Police Services department.
She noted that the City’s partnerships with Illumination Foundation and Mercy House help to take
care of the most vulnerable in the community. Council Member Bucknum encouraged everyone to
verify their voter registration at ocvote.com and to reach out to those relatives that are in assisted
living. She also cautioned residents to protect their ballots. Council Member Bucknum thanked
those that wrote in regarding campaign signs that are posted in prohibited areas and she asked
candidates to be more considerate. Finally, she thanked everyone wo was involved in the renaming
of the Casta del Sol Golf Course and reminded residents that Friday September 11 is Patriots’ Day.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that the COVID cases in ICU are down to 70 which is the
lowest he has seen. He stated that he appreciates everyone’s effort to be safe.

City Council Minutes  6  September 8, 2020
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs said that had no comments this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that she and Mayor Goodell are abiding by the campaign sign policy.
She highlighted the August 28 Medal of Valor Ceremony and pointed out that five Mission Viejo
Deputies received a medal: Deputy Bobby Tomasko received two medals of courage and one medal
of lifesaving; Deputy Nathan Rivas and Deputy Rob White received medals of courage; and Deputy
Alex Santo and Deputy Aaron Grumbles received medals of courage and medals of lifesaving.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also outlined her attendance at the food distribution event at Newhart School
which was sponsored by Saddleback Church. She said she was so impressed with the volunteers
and participants. Lastly, she asked for prayers for all the firefighters that are putting their lives at
risk to distinguish all the fires in California.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked Mayor Pro Tem Kelley for recognizing the recipients of the Medal of Valor
event that they both attended and he stated that the City is very proud of the deputies. During a
conference call regarding homelessness today with Orange County Mayors and City Officials from
across the State, he noted that he shared how Mission Viejo has acquired seven housing units to
assist with transitional housing for people who are in danger of becoming homeless. He also
informed the group that the City funds a Quality of Life Deputy. On that note, he complimented
Quality of Life Deputy Dana Cruz for all the work she has done with the homeless in the City.
Mayor Goodell pointed out that Mission Viejo deputies are not only risking their lives and arresting
criminals, but they are helping people which is so important. He also stated that the City has
expanded the School Resource Officer pool to serve the schools and families. Mayor Goodell
mentioned that there will be upcoming public input meetings on the Vision Program for the Oso
Creek Golf Course and to watch for forthcoming details. Lastly, he stated that he was in a public
service announcement with other County Mayors regarding the usage of masks to help stop the
spread of COVID-19.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 22, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 13, 2020

City Council Minutes  7  September 8, 2020
